pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: app/api/org/members/[userId]/route.ts:56 One PATCH carrying role, status and capabilities commits the role and status writes as separate transactions before the capability write. That write can still refuse with 409 MEMBER_PERMISSIONS_CHANGED (the role change itself moves the editor's expectedCapabilities fingerprint) or last_owner, so the caller gets a refusal while half its request is already durable.

techniques.evidence: app/api/org/members/[userId]/route.ts:56 No unit of work spans the PATCH's three sub-writes. The role commits at :56 and the status at :61, then the IMMEDIATE capability transaction at :103-112 can return 'changed' and answer 409, which is half a unit of work committed. The UI currently sends capabilities alone (MemberPermissionsModal.tsx:58), but the combined body is accepted by the API.

app/api/org/members/[userId]/route.ts:103 The transport handler takes the raw connection from db/core to open its own read-recheck-write transaction instead of calling an org-service operation that owns the boundary. Its sibling guards (underOwnerLock in org-service.ts) live in the service layer.
app/api/org/org-routes.test.ts:2 Route tests run against the real engine via unit-db.ts isolation, not a mocked store.

app/api/repo-scan/route.ts:29 The list response is an explicit per-row field allowlist, never a spread of the store row. The [id] route keeps a second inline copy of the same list ('keep the two lists in lockstep'), so the projection has two definitions, held together only by tests.
